title: Business Registration & Compliance in Nigeria
subtitle: Register your business with the CAC, set up tax and banking correctly, and keep your business legal, trusted and ready for bigger customers.
description: A practical guide for women running small businesses in Nigeria. You will choose between a business name and a limited company under CAMA 2020, register on the CAC portal, confirm your Tax ID, understand when NAFDAC or SON applies, and keep the records and annual returns that keep you compliant. You finish with your own compliance pack and a 90-day plan.
outcomes: Choose between a business name and a private limited company and justify the choice
Prepare and submit a business name registration on the CAC portal, and plan a company incorporation
Set up the essentials after registration: Tax ID, business bank account and safe document storage
Decide whether your products need NAFDAC registration or SON certification and write an honest label
Keep simple records, produce a monthly summary and file annual returns on time
Build a compliance pack, a compliance calendar and a 90-day plan for your own business
audience: Women who already run, or are about to start, a small business in Nigeria and want to register it properly and keep it compliant.
tools: A smartphone or computer with internet access
Your NIN, a passport photograph and a clear signature image
A working email address and phone number in your own name
A notebook or free spreadsheet app for records
Free cloud storage such as Google Drive for your compliance pack

modules.title: Foundations: What Registration and Compliance Really Mean
modules.overview: Before you fill any form, you need to know what the law expects of a small business in Nigeria and which structure fits you. This module explains the regulators you will meet, the difference between a business name and a limited company under CAMA 2020, and how to get your documents and money ready without falling for scams.

lessons.title: Why register, and who regulates a small business in Nigeria
objectives: Explain what the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) does and why registration protects you
Name the main bodies a small business may deal with: CAC, tax authorities, NAFDAC, SON, SMEDAN and your local government
Decide which of these apply to your own business today
Describe what "being compliant" means in practical, everyday terms

blocks.text: Many women in Nigeria run real businesses for years without registering them: a food stall, a tailoring shop, a hair salon, a small soap or zobo brand sold on WhatsApp. The business works, so why bother with forms? The simple answer is that **registration turns your hustle into something the law, banks and big customers can see and trust**. Without it, the business exists only in your head and your phone.

In Nigeria, businesses are registered by the **Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC)**. The CAC keeps the official register of business names and companies under the **Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020 (CAMA 2020)**, the main law on business registration. When you register, the CAC gives you a certificate and a registration number. A business name gets a **BN number** and a company gets an **RC number**. Anyone can search the public register to confirm that your business is real.

blocks.name: businesswoman
blocks.alt: A confident businesswoman standing with her work
blocks.caption: Registration is the step that makes your business visible and trusted, not just a side hustle.

blocks.text: What registration gives you

items: **Protection of your name.** Once your name is registered, another person cannot register the same name with the CAC.
**A business bank account.** Banks ask for CAC documents before opening an account in a business name, so customers can pay "Ada's Kitchen" instead of your personal account.
**Access to bigger customers.** Supermarkets, schools, hotels, companies and government agencies usually ask for CAC documents before they buy from you.
**Access to support.** Many grants, loans, trainings and programmes, including those linked to SMEDAN, ask for registration as proof that you are serious.
**A path to product approval.** NAFDAC asks for evidence of CAC registration before it will register a food, drink or cosmetic product.

head: Body
What it does
When it matters to you

blocks.title: FIRS is now NRS
blocks.text: Under Nigeria's 2025 tax reform laws, which took effect on 1 January 2026, the Federal Inland Revenue Service was replaced by the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS). You may still see "FIRS" on older documents and websites. They refer to the same federal tax role.
What "compliance" means day to day

Compliance sounds like a big word, but for a small business it comes down to a short list of habits. You register correctly. You keep your registration up to date, which mainly means filing **annual returns** with the CAC each year and reporting changes such as a new address. You keep simple records of money in and money out. You register for tax and file what is required, even when the tax due is zero. And if you sell a regulated product, you get the right approval before you sell and you label it honestly.

blocks.title: Worked example: which bodies apply?
blocks.context: For example, Halima runs a small business in Kaduna. She makes groundnut oil and kuli-kuli, packs them in branded bottles and nylon packs, and sells to two supermarkets and on WhatsApp. She also wants a bank loan.
steps: CAC: yes. She needs a registered business so the supermarkets can pay her business account and the bank can lend to the business.
Tax: yes. Once registered, she should confirm her Tax ID and keep records so she can file returns, even if her tax due is small.
NAFDAC: yes. Packaged groundnut oil and kuli-kuli are food products sold to the public, so each product needs NAFDAC registration before supermarket sale.
SON: no. Her products are food, which NAFDAC regulates, so SON certification does not apply to them.
SMEDAN and local government: optional support from SMEDAN; she checks her local government about any permit for her production space.
blocks.result: Halima's compliance list is CAC first, then Tax ID and records, then NAFDAC for each packaged product. Knowing the order stops her from paying for things in the wrong sequence.

blocks.title: Layers of compliance
items: Product approval if regulated
Tax registration and filing
Records and annual returns
CAC registration
blocks.caption: CAC registration is the base; records, tax and product approvals all build on it.

blocks.title: Not every business needs NAFDAC
blocks.text: A tailor, hairdresser, tutor, event planner or phone repairer needs CAC registration and tax, but not NAFDAC. NAFDAC matters when you package food, drinks, cosmetics, chemicals or similar products for sale.

takeaways: The CAC registers businesses under CAMA 2020; you get a BN number (business name) or RC number (company)
Registration protects your name and opens doors to bank accounts, big customers, support and product approval
Compliance is a set of habits: register, file annual returns, keep records, handle tax, approve regulated products
FIRS was replaced by the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) from 1 January 2026

For every "not sure", write the question you need answered (for example, "Does my packaged chin-chin need NAFDAC?").

lessons.title: Business name or limited company: choosing under CAMA 2020
objectives: Explain the difference between a business name and a private limited company
Use key terms correctly: proprietor, partner, director, shareholder, share capital, limited liability
Describe the CAMA 2020 changes that help small businesses, such as the single-member company
Choose the structure that fits a given business and justify the choice

blocks.text: The CAC registers several kinds of entities, but most women starting out choose between two: a **business name** and a **private company limited by shares** (often written "Ltd"). Choosing well saves money now and stress later, so take time to understand both.
Business name: you and your business are one

A business name is the trading name of a person (a **sole proprietor**) or a group of people (a **partnership**). Registering it tells the public who is behind "Ngozi Fabrics". It is simple and usually the cheapest option. But the law does not see the business as separate from you. If the business owes money, **you personally owe it**, and your own property can be used to pay. Income from the business is taxed as your personal income through your State Internal Revenue Service.
Limited company: a separate legal person

A private limited company is a **separate legal person**. It can own property, sign contracts, borrow money and be sued in its own name. The owners are **shareholders**, who hold **shares** in the company. The people who manage it are **directors**. One person can be both. The key benefit is **limited liability**: if the company fails, shareholders generally lose only what they put in, not their personal homes or savings, unless they signed personal guarantees or broke the law.

blocks.name: scales
blocks.caption: Weigh simplicity and low cost against protection and growth when you choose a structure.

blocks.text: What CAMA 2020 changed for small businesses

items: **One person can form a private company.** Under the old law you needed at least two people. Now a single shareholder who is also the director can register a company.
**Minimum share capital is low.** For a private company, CAMA 2020 sets the minimum issued share capital at 100,000 naira, at the time of writing.
**Small companies get lighter rules.** A small private company does not have to appoint a company secretary, and qualifying small companies can be exempt from having their accounts audited.
**Business names now file annual returns too.** CAMA 2020 brought annual returns for business names, not only companies.

blocks.title: Business name vs limited company
items: Business name
Private limited company
blocks.caption: A business name is simpler; a company protects your personal assets and suits growth and investors.

head: Term
Plain meaning

Two or more people running a business name together and sharing profit and liability
A person who owns shares, and so owns part of a company
A person who manages the company and signs on its behalf

blocks.title: Worked example: three women, three choices
blocks.context: For example, three learners in Lagos are deciding on structures. Bisi sells ankara bags from home. Chioma and her sister plan a catering business that will sign contracts with event centres. Funmi is building a small packaged drinks factory and hopes to bring in an investor.
steps: Bisi: low risk, one person, small sales, no big contracts. A business name in her own name is enough for now.
Chioma and her sister: two people, contracts, risk of a large claim if food goes wrong at an event. A private limited company with both as directors and shareholders protects their personal property.
Funmi: equipment loans, an investor who wants a share, and NAFDAC registration. A limited company is the right choice because an investor can only buy shares in a company, not in a business name.
All three note that they can start one way and change later: Bisi can register a company when she grows and move her trading into it.
blocks.result: Bisi registers a business name; Chioma and Funmi register private limited companies. Each choice matches the risk, the number of owners and the growth plan.

blocks.title: Limited liability is not a free pass
blocks.text: If a director signs a personal guarantee for a loan, uses company money for herself, or trades fraudulently, she can still be held personally responsible. Keep company money separate from your own from the first day.

If you are unsure, ask yourself one question: if this business failed tomorrow and owed money, could I pay it from my own pocket without losing my home or savings? If the honest answer is no, and the risks are real, a limited company deserves serious thought even at an early stage.

There are other structures too, such as an incorporated trustee for churches, associations and NGOs, and a limited liability partnership for professionals. If your purpose is charitable or community work rather than profit, ask about incorporated trustees instead of a company.

takeaways: A business name is you trading under a name; you are personally liable for its debts
A private limited company is a separate legal person with limited liability for shareholders
CAMA 2020 allows a one-person company and lighter rules for small companies
Choose based on risk, number of owners, contracts and plans for investors or loans

activity.title: Choose your structure
steps: List your business risks: debts, contracts, products that could harm someone, staff.
Write down how many owners there are now and whether you want an investor in the next two years.
Use the comparison diagram to score business name and company against your answers.
Write a three-sentence decision: structure chosen, the main reason, and what would make you change.
activity.evidence: Your risk list and the three-sentence structure decision, saved as a note or photo.

lessons.title: Getting ready: names, documents, budget and avoiding scams
objectives: Prepare three good name options that are likely to pass the CAC name check
Gather the personal details and documents the CAC portal asks for
Set a realistic budget and timeline using the current official fee schedule
Spot and avoid common registration scams and protect your personal data

blocks.text: Most registration delays happen before the form is even submitted: a name that gets rejected, a missing NIN, a blurry signature, or money paid to the wrong person. A little preparation turns a frustrating week into a smooth afternoon.
Choosing names that pass

The CAC first checks whether your proposed name is available. A name is usually refused if it is identical or too similar to an existing registered name, if it is offensive or misleading, or if it uses restricted words without approval. Words that suggest a link to government, such as **Federal, National, State or Government**, need consent. Words tied to regulated sectors, such as **Bank, Insurance or Microfinance**, need approval from the regulator of that sector.

items: Prepare **three options**, from your favourite to your back-up.
Make each name distinctive: add a local word, your own name, or a clear product word, such as "Amaka Okoro Kitchen" rather than "Good Food".
For a company, the name must end with "Limited" or "Ltd".
Search the public register on the CAC website first to see if a similar name already exists.

blocks.text: Budget and timeline

CAC fees, and the time it takes to approve applications, change from time to time. Always read the **current fee shown on the CAC portal at the point of payment**, and be wary of any website that quotes a fixed official price. A company costs more than a business name, and part of a company's cost depends on its share capital, because stamp duty is charged on it. If you use an agent, their professional fee is separate from the CAC fee, so ask for a written breakdown.

blocks.title: Worked example: planning a registration budget
blocks.context: For example, Esther in Ibadan has 60,000 naira set aside and wants a business name for her small bakery, with her first supermarket meeting in three weeks.
steps: She logs into the CAC portal and notes the business name fee shown for her application, rather than trusting a figure from a blog.
She adds a small amount for data and printing, and a few thousand naira for passport photos.
She keeps the rest as a buffer in case her first name is rejected and she has to resubmit.
She starts the registration this week, because approval can take several working days and she wants the certificate before the meeting.
blocks.result: Esther's budget is based on the official figure on the day she pays, with a buffer, and her timeline leaves room for a rejected name.

blocks.title: Avoid registration scams
blocks.text: Pay CAC fees only through the official portal's payment page. Be careful with people on social media promising "same day CAC" for cash to a personal account, or asking for your NIN, BVN, bank PIN or OTP. The CAC will never need your bank PIN or OTP. If you use an agent, ask for their accreditation and check it on the CAC website, and insist that the business is registered in **your** name with **your** email.
Doing it yourself or paying for help

You can register a business name yourself if you are comfortable with forms on your phone. Paying an accredited agent makes more sense for a company, for partnerships with several owners, or if your time is worth more than the fee. Either way, you remain the owner, so read every page before it is submitted and keep copies of everything that was filed in your name.

Your NIN, photo, signature and address are valuable personal data. Send them only through the official portal or to an agent you have checked, never in an open WhatsApp group. After registration, keep copies of everything in one safe folder. You will learn to build that folder later in the course.

takeaways: Prepare three distinctive names and avoid restricted words such as Federal, National, Bank or Insurance without approval
Have NIN, passport photo, signature, addresses, email and phone ready before you start
Use the fee shown on the official CAC portal at payment, not figures from blogs
Never share your bank PIN or OTP; make sure the business is registered in your own name and email

Confirm your NIN details match your other documents.

quiz.q: Amina sells packaged zobo drinks to shops. Which order of compliance steps makes the most sense?
options: NAFDAC first, then CAC, then tax
CAC registration first, then Tax ID and records, then NAFDAC product registration
quiz.explain: NAFDAC asks for evidence of CAC registration, so CAC comes first. Tax registration and records follow registration, and packaged drinks then need NAFDAC approval.

quiz.q: What is the main legal risk of trading as a business name rather than a limited company?
options: You cannot open any bank account
You are personally liable for the business's debts
You must have an audit every year
quiz.explain: A business name is not separate from its owner, so the owner's personal property can be used to pay business debts.

quiz.q: Under CAMA 2020, which statement about forming a private company is correct?
options: At least two shareholders are always required
A single person can be the only shareholder and director
Only Nigerian banks can form companies
A company secretary is compulsory for every small company
quiz.explain: CAMA 2020 allows a one-person private company, and small private companies do not have to appoint a company secretary.

quiz.q: Joy wants to name her business "Federal Quality Foods". What is the most likely problem?
options: "Federal" suggests a government link and needs consent
quiz.explain: Words that suggest government connection, such as Federal or National, are restricted and need consent before they can be used.

quiz.q: Someone on Facebook offers "same day CAC" and asks for your NIN, BVN and the OTP sent to your phone. What should you do?
options: Send everything quickly to save time
Refuse; pay only through the official portal and never share PINs or OTPs
Pay half now and half later
quiz.explain: OTPs and PINs give access to your bank. Legitimate registration never needs them, and CAC fees should be paid through the official portal.

quiz.q: A tailor who sews to order in her shop wants to be compliant. Which body is she least likely to need?
options: Her local government for a shop permit or signage
quiz.explain: NAFDAC regulates food, drinks, cosmetics, drugs and chemicals. A tailoring service does not fall under NAFDAC.

modules.title: Guided Practice: Registering and Setting Up Properly
modules.overview: This module walks you through the actual registration work. You will follow the steps for a business name on the CAC portal, plan the key decisions for a private limited company, and complete the set-up tasks that come after the certificate: Tax ID, business bank account and safe storage of your documents.

lessons.title: Registering a business name on the CAC portal, step by step
objectives: Create an account on the CAC Company Registration Portal and run a name availability check
Complete the business name registration form accurately
Pay through the portal and track your application
Respond correctly to a query or rejection

blocks.text: The CAC handles registration online through its **Company Registration Portal (CRP)**, which you reach from the official website, cac.gov.ng. You can register a business name yourself from a phone or computer. The screens change from time to time, so treat the steps below as the logic of the process, and follow the labels you see on the portal on the day.

blocks.name: complete-form
blocks.alt: A woman completing an online form
blocks.caption: Most of the registration work is filling one online form carefully and correctly.

blocks.text: The workflow

blocks.title: Business name registration flow
items: Create portal account
Check name availability
Fill registration form
Pay on portal
Respond to any query
Download certificate
blocks.caption: Each step depends on the one before it, so do not skip the name check.

items: **Create your account.** Sign up on the CAC portal with your own email address and phone number, then verify the email. Write your password somewhere safe.

**Check and reserve the name.** Choose business name registration, enter your first name option and the type of business. The system checks availability. If it is approved, you can proceed with that name. If not, try your next option.

**Fill the registration form.** Enter the business address, the nature of the business, the start date, and the details of each proprietor or partner: full name as on NIN, date of birth, contact and residential address.
**Upload documents.** Add each proprietor's passport photograph and signature image where requested, and confirm identity details against the NIN.
**Review before paying.** Check every spelling, especially your names and the business name. Errors after approval are harder and costlier to fix.
**Pay the fee on the portal.** Use the payment option on the portal and keep the receipt or payment reference.
**Track and respond.** Check your email and the portal dashboard. If the CAC raises a query, read it, correct exactly what is asked and resubmit.
**Download your documents.** When approved, download the certificate and registration details and save them in your compliance folder.

blocks.text: Writing a good "nature of business"

The nature of business tells the public and regulators what you do. A vague description like "general business" can cause a query and can confuse a bank or NAFDAC later. Write it in simple words that match what you actually sell, and include closely related activities you plan within the next year or two. For example: "Production, packaging and sale of snacks and soft drinks, and outdoor catering services."

blocks.title: Worked example: fixing a query
blocks.context: For example, Kemi in Abeokuta submitted a business name application for "Kemi's Hair Hub". Three working days later she received an email: the uploaded signature was not clear and her surname was spelt differently from her NIN record.
steps: She reads the query carefully and notes the two problems: unclear signature, surname mismatch.
She signs again on clean white paper with a black pen, photographs it in daylight and crops it tightly.
She opens the application from her dashboard and corrects her surname to match the NIN exactly, letter for letter.
She uploads the new signature, resubmits, and saves a screenshot of the resubmission page.
Two days later the application is approved and she downloads her certificate.
blocks.result: Kemi fixed only what the query asked for, kept proof of resubmission, and got approval without paying again.

blocks.title: Record everything as you go
blocks.text: Screenshot the name approval, the completed form summary, the payment receipt and the approval email. If anything goes wrong, these screenshots are your proof when you contact the CAC help desk.
Common mistakes
What happens after you submit

Once you pay, your application joins a queue for review by CAC staff. They check that the name is acceptable, that your identity details match, and that the uploads are clear. You will see the status change on your dashboard, and you will usually receive emails at each stage. Approval time varies with demand, so do not promise a customer a date that depends on CAC approval.

items: **Approved:** download the certificate and registration details immediately and save them in two places.
**Queried:** read the query, fix only what is asked, and resubmit from the same application. You do not pay again for a query.
**Rejected name:** go back to your list of three names and try the next option.
**Stuck for a long time:** contact the CAC help desk through the official website, quoting your application or payment reference.

blocks.text: Keep the payment reference safe. It is the fastest way for the CAC to find your application if you need help, and it proves you paid through the official channel.

items: Registering with an agent's email or phone, so all notices go to someone else.
Using a nickname instead of the name on your NIN.
A blurry or oversized photo or signature file.
Choosing a name you have not searched, leading to repeated rejections.
Paying someone outside the portal and receiving no official receipt.

takeaways: Business names can be registered by the owner on the CAC Company Registration Portal
The order is account, name check, form, upload, review, pay, respond, download
Your details must match your NIN exactly
Answer queries by fixing exactly what is asked and keep screenshots of each step
