lessons.title: Incorporating a private limited company: shares, directors and decisions
objectives: Decide the share capital and how shares are split between owners
Identify who will be directors, shareholders and persons with significant control
Describe the steps and documents in company incorporation
Explain when to use an accredited agent and what to check

blocks.text: Registering a company asks you to make decisions that a business name does not: how many shares to create, who owns them, who will be a director, and what rules will govern the company. These decisions affect control, tax, cost and future investment, so make them with a pen and a calculator before you open the portal.
The main decisions

items: **Company name** ending in "Limited" or "Ltd", checked and reserved on the portal.
**Registered office address** in Nigeria where official letters can reach the company.
**Share capital**: the number of shares and their value. For a private company, CAMA 2020 sets a minimum issued share capital of 100,000 naira at the time of writing.
**Shareholders** and how many shares each holds.
**Directors**: at least one for a small private company; each must be an adult and give identity details.
**Persons with significant control (PSC)**: people who ultimately own or control a significant share, who must be disclosed.
**Objects of the company**: what the company is set up to do, in clear words.
**Memorandum and Articles of Association**: the founding document. The CAC portal offers standard model articles, which suit most small companies.

blocks.name: business-decisions
blocks.caption: Share and director decisions are made by the owners together, before registration.

blocks.text: How shares translate into control

Shares are a simple way to divide ownership. If a company issues 1,000,000 shares of 1 naira each, its issued share capital is 1,000,000 naira. A person holding 600,000 of those shares owns 60 percent. Ownership affects voting at general meetings and who receives dividends. Stamp duty is charged on share capital at registration, so a bigger share capital costs more to register. Choose a figure you can justify, not the biggest number you can think of.

blocks.title: Worked example: splitting shares between sisters
blocks.context: For example, Chioma and her sister Adaeze in Enugu are registering "Ada & Chioma Catering Ltd". Chioma will run the business full time and put in 700,000 naira of equipment and cash. Adaeze will contribute 300,000 naira and help at weekends.
steps: They choose an issued share capital of 1,000,000 naira, made of 1,000,000 ordinary shares of 1 naira each, matching their total contribution.
Chioma takes 700,000 shares (70 percent) and Adaeze takes 300,000 shares (30 percent).
Both sisters become directors so either can sign for the company, with a rule that payments above an agreed amount need both signatures.
Chioma, with 70 percent, is listed as a person with significant control; they check the portal for whether Adaeze's 30 percent also needs to be disclosed, and complete the PSC section accordingly.
They adopt the standard model articles and write a short private agreement on what happens if one sister wants to leave.
blocks.result: The share split reflects what each sister put in, control is clear, and both can sign. The company is registered with share capital the sisters can explain to a bank.

blocks.title: Company incorporation timeline
items: Agree shares and directors
Reserve company name
Complete incorporation form
Pay fees and stamp duty
Certificate and status report
blocks.caption: Most of the hard thinking happens before the form; the portal steps follow your decisions.

blocks.text: Doing it yourself or using an accredited agent

Company registration involves more legal choices than a business name. Many owners use an **accredited agent**, such as a lawyer, chartered accountant or chartered secretary accredited by the CAC, to prepare and file the application. An agent can save time and avoid mistakes in the PSC section and articles. If you use one, protect yourself.

head: Ask the agent
Why it matters
rows: Are you accredited by the CAC? What is your accreditation number?
You can confirm it on the CAC website
Will the portal account and email be mine?
You must receive notices and control the company records
Can I see the CAC fee and your professional fee separately, in writing?
Will you send me the full set of documents after approval?
You need the certificate, status report and Memorandum and Articles
Who will file my annual returns, and when?

blocks.text: Write down what the articles do not say

Standard model articles cover how the company is run, but they do not cover private matters between owners: what happens if one owner leaves, how profits are shared beyond dividends, or who may sell shares to whom. A short **shareholders' agreement**, written and signed by all owners, prevents painful disputes later, especially between family members and friends. A lawyer can help, but even a simple signed page is better than nothing.

blocks.title: No nominee "fronting"
blocks.text: Do not let someone else register the company in their name "on your behalf". The person on the register is the legal owner. Women have lost businesses this way. Your name, your NIN, your shares.

takeaways: A private company needs a name ending in Limited, an address, share capital, shareholders, at least one director and disclosed PSCs
Shares divide ownership; 700,000 of 1,000,000 shares means 70 percent
Stamp duty depends on share capital, so choose a figure you can justify
If you use an agent, confirm accreditation and keep the account and email in your name

activity.title: Draft your company decision sheet
steps: Write your proposed company name with "Limited" and two back-ups.
Decide total issued share capital and write the number of shares and value per share.
List each shareholder with number of shares and percentage, and check the percentages add up to 100.
List directors and persons with significant control.
Write one sentence for the company objects.
activity.evidence: A one-page company decision sheet with names, share table adding to 100 percent, directors, PSCs and objects.

lessons.title: After the certificate: Tax ID, bank account and safe documents
objectives: List the documents you should receive after CAC approval and check them for errors
Explain how Tax ID registration works for individuals and registered businesses at the time of writing
Open a business bank account and keep business money separate
Store registration documents safely and verify your business on the public register

blocks.text: Getting the certificate is not the finish line. The next two weeks decide whether your registration actually helps you. Check your documents, get your tax identity in order, open a business account, and file everything safely.
Check what you received

items: **Certificate of registration** showing your business name or company name and BN or RC number.
**Registration details or status report** listing proprietors, or for a company, directors, shareholders, share capital and registered address.
For a company, the **Memorandum and Articles of Association**.

blocks.text: Read every line. Check spellings of names, the address and, for companies, the share numbers. If there is an error, raise it with the CAC quickly through the portal or help desk, because the details on the register are what banks and customers rely on. Then search your business on the CAC public search to confirm it appears correctly.

blocks.name: identification-card
blocks.caption: Your NIN and your CAC number together form the basis of your tax identity.

blocks.text: Tax ID: how it works now

Every taxpayer needs a tax identity. Under the **Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025**, part of the reform laws that took effect on 1 January 2026, Nigeria is moving to a single **Tax ID** system. At the time of writing, individuals are identified through their **NIN**, and businesses registered with the CAC are identified through their **registration number**. Companies registered through the CAC have, for some years, been issued a Tax Identification Number (TIN) as part of incorporation. Because the rollout is recent, check your Tax ID status on the official channels of the Nigeria Revenue Service or the Joint Revenue Board before filing anything.

head: Structure
Tax identity
Who you file with
rows: Your personal Tax ID (linked to NIN); the business name is part of your personal tax affairs
Your State Internal Revenue Service, for personal income tax
The company's own Tax ID linked to its RC number
Nigeria Revenue Service, for company income tax and VAT

blocks.text: Open a business bank account

Take your CAC documents, your valid ID and BVN to a bank or licensed microfinance or digital bank that offers business accounts. Requirements differ by bank, so ask for their checklist first. A company account usually needs the details of all directors and sometimes a board resolution authorising the account. Once it is open, **send all business income into it and pay business expenses from it.** This one habit makes record keeping, tax and loan applications far easier.

blocks.title: Worked example: separating money in month one
blocks.context: For example, Rukayat in Ilorin registered "Rukky Bakes" as a business name and opened a business account. In her first month she received 185,000 naira from customers and spent 112,000 naira on flour, sugar, gas and packaging.
steps: She gives customers only the business account number and her Moniepoint business POS for card payments.
She pays suppliers from the business account and keeps every receipt in an envelope labelled with the month.
At the end of the month she pays herself a fixed 40,000 naira transfer to her personal account, recorded as "owner's drawings".
Her business account shows 185,000 in, 112,000 out for costs, 40,000 out as drawings, leaving 33,000 naira in the business.
blocks.result: Rukayat can see her real profit (185,000 minus 112,000 equals 73,000 naira) and what she took home, and her bank statement now supports any loan or tax filing.

blocks.title: First two weeks after approval
items: Check documents for errors
Confirm on public search
Confirm Tax ID
Open business account
File documents safely
blocks.caption: Do these five steps in order so every later task rests on correct records.

blocks.text: Checking a business on the public search

The CAC public search on the official website lets anyone look up a registered business by name or registration number. Use it in two ways. First, to confirm your own record is correct and shows the right status. Second, to check suppliers, partners or agents before you pay them: if a company says it is registered but you cannot find it, ask questions before sending money.

If your Tax ID details are wrong, for example the name on the tax record does not match your NIN or certificate, raise it early through the official NRS or state tax channels. A mismatch can cause problems later when you file returns or apply for tax clearance.

Finally, update your invoices, receipts, WhatsApp Business profile and labels so that they show your registered name exactly as it appears on the certificate. For a company, it is good practice to show the RC number on invoices too. Consistent details make it easy for customers and banks to match your business to the register.

blocks.title: Keep three copies
blocks.text: Save your certificate and status report as PDFs in two places, for example Google Drive and a memory card, and keep one printed copy in a plastic folder. Lost documents can be re-obtained, but it costs time and money.

takeaways: Check every detail on your certificate and status report, and confirm the business on the public search
From 2026 the Tax ID system links individuals to NIN and businesses to their CAC number; confirm status on official channels
Business names are taxed through the owner's state tax authority; companies through the NRS
Open a business account and keep business and personal money separate from day one

activity.title: Complete your after-registration set-up
steps: Check your certificate and status report line by line and note any errors.
Search your business on the CAC public search and take a screenshot.
Find out your Tax ID status through the official NRS or JRB channel and note it.
Ask one bank for its business account checklist, or open the account if you are ready.
Save your documents in two digital places and one printed folder.
activity.evidence: Screenshot of your public search result, a note of your Tax ID status, and a photo of your document folder or bank checklist.

quiz.q: Kemi's business name application is queried because her surname differs from her NIN record. What should she do?
options: Start a new application with a new name
Correct the surname to match the NIN exactly and resubmit
Ignore the query; it will be approved later
Ask a friend to register it instead
quiz.explain: The portal checks identity against the NIN, so the fix is to match the NIN spelling exactly and resubmit through the same application.

quiz.q: A company issues 1,000,000 shares. Ifeoma holds 250,000. What percentage does she own?
quiz.explain: 250,000 divided by 1,000,000 equals 0.25, which is 25 percent.

quiz.q: Why should you not choose a very large share capital "to look big"?
options: CAC forbids share capital above 100,000 naira
Stamp duty at registration rises with share capital
It makes the company a business name
quiz.explain: Stamp duty is charged on share capital, so a larger figure costs more to register. Choose a figure you can justify.

quiz.q: Which is the best description for "nature of business" on a registration form?
options: Production, packaging and sale of snacks and soft drinks
quiz.explain: A specific description that matches what you sell avoids queries and helps banks and regulators understand your business.

quiz.q: Ngozi registered a business name. Where does she file tax on its profits?
options: Nigeria Revenue Service as company income tax
Her State Internal Revenue Service as personal income tax
quiz.explain: A business name is not a separate legal person, so its profit is the owner's personal income, handled by the state tax authority.

quiz.q: An agent offers to register your company using their own email and portal account. What is the risk?
options: Notices and control of records go to the agent, not you
The company will pay less tax
quiz.explain: Whoever controls the account and email receives notices and can act on the records. Keep the account in your own name and email.

modules.title: Staying Compliant: Annual Returns, Product Rules and Records
modules.overview: Registration is a one-time event; compliance is a habit. This module covers what you must keep doing after registration: filing annual returns, meeting product rules from NAFDAC or SON, treating customers and their data fairly, and keeping simple records that support your tax filings and show how the business is really doing.

lessons.title: Annual returns, changes and the most common compliance mistakes
objectives: Explain what an annual return is and when companies and business names must file
Know which changes must be reported to the CAC, such as address or directors
Recognise the most common compliance mistakes and their consequences
Check your own business status on the CAC public search

blocks.text: An **annual return** is a yearly update you file with the CAC to confirm that your business still exists and that its details are correct. It is not the same as a tax return. Think of it as telling the register, once a year, "we are still here, and this is who we are".

blocks.name: spiral-calendar-pad
blocks.caption: Annual returns come round every year, so they belong on your calendar.

blocks.text: Who files what

head: Structure
What the annual return covers
Timing
rows: Registered address, directors, shareholders and share capital, persons with significant control, and financial statements (small companies may qualify for simpler, unaudited accounts)
Every year; the first is due not later than 18 months after incorporation
Confirmation of the proprietors or partners and details of the business, including a statement of its turnover or activity
Every year, as required by CAMA 2020; check the portal for the current due date

blocks.text: Annual returns are filed on the CAC portal, the same place you registered. Late filing attracts **penalties for each year missed**, and a company that does not file for a long time can be marked inactive and may eventually be struck off the register. A struck-off business cannot use its registration to open accounts, bid for contracts or apply for NAFDAC approval until it is restored.

blocks.title: Fees and penalty amounts
blocks.text: The filing fee and the late-filing penalty are set by the CAC and can change. Use the figure shown on the portal when you file, and treat any amount quoted on social media as unconfirmed.
Changes you must report

items: A new business address or registered office.
A new director or proprietor, or one leaving.
A transfer of shares, or new shares being issued.
A change of company or business name.
A change in persons with significant control.

blocks.text: Each change has its own filing on the portal, and some have deadlines in CAMA 2020. Report changes promptly, because banks, customers and regulators trust what the register says, not what you tell them. If the register says your sister is still a director after she has left, she may still be able to sign documents in the company's name.
The most common mistakes

blocks.title: How small mistakes grow
items: Return not filed
Penalties build up
Status shows inactive
Bank or buyer refuses
Costly catch-up filing
blocks.caption: One missed filing can block a loan or contract months later, so break the cycle early.

items: **Thinking registration is the end.** Many owners register, then never file an annual return.
**Mixing money.** Business income goes into a personal account, so there is no clean record to support filings.
**Letting an agent hold the account.** The agent moves on and the owner cannot log in to file.
**Not reporting changes.** Old directors and addresses stay on the register for years.
**Selling a regulated product before approval.** Packaged food or cosmetics sold without a NAFDAC number can be seized and the business penalised.

blocks.title: Worked example: catching up on missed returns
blocks.context: For example, Grace registered "Grace Fashion Ltd" in Port Harcourt more than three years ago and never filed an annual return. A hotel now wants to award her a uniform contract and asks for her CAC status report.
steps: She searches her company on the CAC public search. The status shows the company is not up to date.
She logs into the portal with the email used at registration and sees the annual returns that are outstanding, year by year.
She gathers the details for each year: directors, shareholders, address and simple financial statements prepared from her bank statements and sales book.
She files the outstanding returns in order and pays the filing fees and late penalties shown on the portal.
She downloads an updated status report and sends it to the hotel, then sets a yearly reminder on her phone.
blocks.result: Grace keeps the contract, but she pays penalties she could have avoided. Her new yearly reminder means it will not happen again.

blocks.text: Preparing the figures

The financial part of an annual return is where many owners panic, but if you kept records through the year it is mostly copying. For a business name, you need a summary of turnover and activity for the year. For a company, you need financial statements. CAMA 2020 lets qualifying small companies use simpler, unaudited accounts, but the figures must still be true and come from your records and bank statements. If you are unsure, a chartered accountant can prepare the statements from your monthly summaries for a fee.

Remember that the annual return is filed by the business, not by the agent who registered it. If someone else handled your registration, ask now for the login details or move the business to an account you control.

blocks.title: Check your status today
blocks.text: Search your business on the CAC public search and look at its status. If anything looks wrong or out of date, fix it now, before a bank or customer finds it first.

takeaways: An annual return is a yearly CAC update, separate from a tax return
Companies file every year, the first within 18 months of incorporation; business names also file under CAMA 2020
Report changes to address, directors, shares, name or PSCs on the portal
Late filing brings penalties and can block loans, contracts and NAFDAC applications

activity.title: Run a status check
steps: Search your business (or a business you know) on the CAC public search and note its status.
Write down your registration date and work out when your next annual return is due.
List any changes since registration that have not been reported.
Set a phone reminder one month before the next annual return is due.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of the public search result and a note of your next filing date and any unreported changes.

lessons.title: Products, people and data: NAFDAC, SON, honest labels and fair dealing
objectives: Decide whether a product needs NAFDAC registration or SON certification
Describe the NAFDAC small business (MSME) registration process and documents
Write a label that is honest and complete
Handle customer data and business relationships fairly and safely

blocks.text: Compliance is not only paperwork. It is about making sure the people who buy from you are safe, are told the truth and have their information protected. That is also good business: trust is what brings customers back.
NAFDAC or SON?

**NAFDAC** (the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) regulates food, drinks, packaged water, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices and chemicals. If you package any of these for sale to the public, the product needs NAFDAC registration and a NAFDAC number on the label. **SON** (the Standards Organisation of Nigeria) sets Nigerian Industrial Standards and certifies locally manufactured products that NAFDAC does not regulate, through its MANCAP certification scheme. A product is regulated by one or the other, not both.

blocks.title: Which regulator for my product?
items: Is it packaged for sale?
Food, drink, cosmetic, chemical?
Yes: NAFDAC registration
Other manufactured goods: check SON
Service only: CAC and tax
blocks.caption: Start with what you sell; the product type tells you which regulator applies.

blocks.text: The NAFDAC MSME route

NAFDAC has a dedicated route for micro and small enterprises. Its published procedure for registering MSME products lists these main stages: apply on the NAFDAC website or through a state office, submit documents and pay, book a facility inspection at a date you choose, have samples taken for laboratory analysis during the inspection, and collect your certificate once the inspection and lab results are satisfactory. The same document gives a target of **90 working days** from application to certificate.

items: Evidence of CAC registration.
Trademark approval documentation for your brand name.
A site use agreement where you do not own the premises.
A vetting sample and labels.
A fumigation certificate for the production premises.
Food handler or medical fitness certificates for production staff.
The payment receipt.

blocks.name: label
blocks.caption: An honest, complete label is part of compliance and part of your brand.

blocks.text: Honest, complete labels

A food or cosmetic label should tell the buyer what the product is, what is in it, how much is in it, who made it and where, the NAFDAC number, the batch number, and the manufacturing and expiry dates. Never print a NAFDAC number you have not been given, and never copy another brand's number. Avoid health claims such as "cures typhoid" or "reduces sugar": claims like these need evidence and approval, and false claims mislead people who may be sick.

blocks.title: Worked example: fixing a label before NAFDAC
blocks.context: For example, Ifeyinwa in Owerri makes a pepper sauce. Her current sticker says "Ify's Hot Sauce, 100% natural, boosts immunity, NAFDAC approved". She has not yet applied to NAFDAC.
steps: She removes "NAFDAC approved" immediately, because she has no NAFDAC number yet.
She removes "boosts immunity", a health claim she cannot prove.
She adds the ingredients in order of quantity, the net content (for example, 250 ml), her business name and address, and space for the NAFDAC number, batch number and dates.
She registers "Ify's Hot Sauce" as a business name, starts the trademark process, and prepares the MSME application documents.
blocks.result: Her label is now honest and ready for NAFDAC review, and she avoids the risk of having products seized for false claims.

blocks.text: Customer data and fair dealing

The **Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023**, enforced by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, protects personal information such as names, phone numbers, addresses and payment details. For a small business, follow simple rules: collect only what you need, tell customers why you are collecting it, do not add people to broadcast lists without their agreement, keep customer lists on a phone or account with a password, and never share someone's details with another business without their consent.
Protecting your brand name

Registering a business name with the CAC protects the name on the business register, but it does not by itself protect a product brand or logo. Brand names and logos are protected as **trademarks**, through the Trademarks, Patents and Designs Registry under the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment. NAFDAC's MSME procedure lists trademark documentation among its requirements, so start the trademark process early.
Fair dealing with customers

items: Show clear prices and say upfront whether delivery is included.
Give a receipt or invoice for every sale, with your registered business name on it.
State your refund or replacement policy before payment, especially for online orders.
If a customer reports a problem with a food or cosmetic product, record the batch number, stop selling that batch until you understand the problem, and respond respectfully.

blocks.title: Protect your own position as a woman owner
blocks.text: Register the business in your own name, keep your own login details, and be a signatory on the business bank account. If a husband, partner or relative is a co-owner, write the share split and roles down. Clear records protect everyone and prevent disputes about who owns what.

takeaways: NAFDAC regulates packaged food, drinks, cosmetics, drugs and chemicals; SON certifies other manufactured goods through MANCAP
The NAFDAC MSME route needs CAC registration, trademark documents, inspection and lab tests; its published target is 90 working days
Labels must be truthful: never show a NAFDAC number you do not have, and avoid unproven health claims
Handle customer data with consent and care under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023

activity.title: Audit one product and one customer list
steps: Pick one product you sell and decide: NAFDAC, SON, or neither.
Write out its label and mark any missing item or unproven claim.
If NAFDAC applies, list which MSME documents you already have and which you still need.
Look at how you store customer phone numbers and write two changes that would protect them better.
activity.evidence: A photo of your corrected label draft, your NAFDAC document checklist (if relevant), and your two data protection changes.

lessons.title: Simple record keeping and tax basics that support compliance
objectives: Keep a simple sales and expenses record that supports tax and annual returns
Produce a monthly summary showing sales, costs and profit
Explain the main taxes a small business may meet under the 2025 reform laws
Use three simple numbers to measure how the business is doing

blocks.text: Records are the evidence behind every compliance task. Your annual return needs figures, your tax filing needs figures, and your bank wants figures before a loan. You do not need accounting software to start. A notebook, an exercise book or a free spreadsheet on your phone is enough if you use it every day.
The four records to keep

items: **Sales record:** date, customer or channel, item, quantity, amount, and how paid (cash, transfer, POS).
**Expenses record:** date, supplier, item, amount, and whether you kept a receipt.
**Receipts and invoices:** paper receipts in a monthly envelope, or photos in a monthly phone folder.
**Bank statements:** download your business account statement each month.

blocks.text: CAMA 2020 requires companies to keep proper accounting records, and to keep them for six years. Business name owners should keep records for the same length of time, because tax authorities can ask about earlier years. Paper fades and phones get lost, so back up photos and spreadsheets to cloud storage.

blocks.name: ledger
blocks.caption: A simple daily ledger is the evidence behind your tax filing and annual return.

blocks.text: Your monthly summary

blocks.title: Worked example: one month for a small bakery
blocks.context: For example, Rukayat's bakery in Ilorin recorded these figures in March (approximate naira).
steps: Total sales from her sales record: 420,000 naira (cash 90,000, transfers 250,000, POS 80,000).
Direct costs (flour, sugar, butter, eggs, packaging): 231,000 naira. Gross profit = 420,000 minus 231,000 = 189,000 naira.
Gross margin = 189,000 divided by 420,000 = 45 percent.
Other costs (gas, transport, data, stall levy): 64,000 naira. Net profit = 189,000 minus 64,000 = 125,000 naira.
She compares the 340,000 naira of transfers and POS with her bank statement and finds they match, so her records are complete.
blocks.result: Rukayat knows she made about 125,000 naira profit in March, at a 45 percent gross margin, and has records she can show the tax office or a bank.

blocks.title: From daily records to compliance
items: Daily sales and expenses
Monthly summary
Yearly accounts
Tax filing and annual return
blocks.caption: Small daily entries add up to the yearly figures every filing needs.

blocks.text: Tax basics after the 2025 reforms

Nigeria's new tax laws took effect on 1 January 2026, so expect guidance to keep developing. At the time of writing, the main points for small businesses are these. A **company** files company income tax returns with the Nigeria Revenue Service. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a company that meets the legal definition of a **small company**, based on limits on its turnover and fixed assets, pays company income tax at **0 percent** and is excluded from the development levy, but it must still file. Check the current limits with the NRS, because definitions can be updated. A **business name** owner pays personal income tax on her business profit through her State Internal Revenue Service. **VAT** applies to many goods and services at 7.5 percent, but very small businesses below the legal threshold are not required to charge it. If you employ staff, you also deduct **PAYE** tax from their pay and remit it to the state.

blocks.title: Zero tax is not zero filing
blocks.text: Even when the tax due is nothing, filing a return is what proves you are compliant. Not filing can lead to penalties and makes it harder to get a tax clearance certificate, which contracts and loans often ask for.
Three numbers to watch every month
A simple cash book layout

head: Date
Details
Money in
Money out
How paid
rows: Sold 20 loaves to Mama Tunde's shop

blocks.text: Write in the cash book the same day, while you remember. At the end of each week, count your cash and compare it with the cash column. If there is a difference, write a note explaining it. Small daily discipline is what makes your yearly figures believable to a tax officer or a bank.
Making records easier

items: Use one business account for all digital payments so your bank statement does half of the record keeping for you.
Ask suppliers for receipts every time; if they have none, write your own note with date, item, amount and supplier name, and sign it.
Photograph paper receipts on the day and save them in a monthly folder on your phone.
Note what you take for yourself as "owner's drawings", not as a business expense, so your profit figure stays true.
Set a fixed time each week, for example Sunday evening, to bring the records up to date.

head: Measure
How to calculate
What it tells you
rows: (Sales minus direct costs) divided by sales
Whether your prices cover your materials
Transfers and POS in records compared with bank statement
Whether your records are complete enough to rely on

takeaways: Keep four records: sales, expenses, receipts and bank statements, and back them up
CAMA 2020 requires companies to keep accounting records for six years
A small company pays 0 percent company income tax under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 but must still file
Watch monthly sales, gross margin and whether your records match your bank statement

activity.title: Make your first monthly summary
steps: Set up a sales page and an expenses page in a notebook or spreadsheet.
Record every sale and expense for at least one week (one month if you can).
Add up sales, direct costs and other costs, and calculate gross profit, gross margin and net profit.
Compare transfers and POS in your records with your bank statement and note any gap.
activity.evidence: A photo or screenshot of your records and monthly summary with the three numbers calculated.

quiz.q: Grace's company was incorporated in January 2025. By when must its first annual return be filed?
options: Not later than 18 months after incorporation
Only when the company makes a profit
Never; only business names file annual returns
quiz.explain: Under CAMA 2020, a company's first annual return is due not later than 18 months after incorporation, then every year.

quiz.q: Ifeyinwa's pepper sauce label says "NAFDAC approved" but she has not applied yet. What should she do first?
options: Remove the claim immediately and apply properly
Change it to "NAFDAC pending" and keep selling to supermarkets
quiz.explain: Showing approval you do not have is false and illegal. Remove it and follow the NAFDAC registration process.

quiz.q: Which product is most likely to need SON certification rather than NAFDAC registration?
quiz.explain: Food, cosmetics and packaged water are NAFDAC-regulated. Manufactured goods outside NAFDAC's remit, such as electrical products, fall under SON standards and certification.

quiz.q: A bakery has sales of 300,000 naira and direct costs of 180,000 naira. What is its gross margin?
quiz.explain: Gross profit is 300,000 minus 180,000 = 120,000. 120,000 divided by 300,000 = 0.4, or 40 percent.

quiz.q: A small company owes 0 percent company income tax this year. What should it do?
options: Nothing, since no tax is due
Still file its tax return with the NRS
Register as a business name instead
quiz.explain: A 0 percent rate does not remove the duty to file. Filing proves compliance and supports a tax clearance certificate.

quiz.q: A customer gave you her phone number to arrange delivery. Under good data practice, what should you avoid?
options: Saving it in a password-protected phone
Using it to arrange the delivery
Adding her to a promotional broadcast list without asking
Deleting it when no longer needed
quiz.explain: The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 expects you to use data for the purpose given and get consent for other uses, such as marketing.

modules.title: Your Compliance Pack: Proof, Trust and a 90-Day Plan
modules.overview: In this final module you bring everything together. You will build a compliance pack that holds every key document, learn to use your registration to win customers, loans and support, and finish with a compliance calendar and a 90-day plan that keeps your business in good standing.

lessons.title: Building your business compliance pack
objectives: List the documents that belong in a compliance pack for a business name or company
Organise the pack in paper and digital form so anything can be found in two minutes
Run a gap check and plan how to fill each gap
Protect sensitive documents from loss and misuse

blocks.text: A **compliance pack** is one organised folder that holds every document proving your business is registered, up to date and allowed to sell what it sells. When a supermarket, bank, grant officer or NAFDAC inspector asks for something, you should be able to send it the same day. It is also the main part of your capstone project for this course.

blocks.name: folder-files
blocks.alt: A person organising files in folders
blocks.caption: One well-organised folder replaces hours of searching for documents.

blocks.text: What goes in the pack

head: Section
Documents
Applies to
rows: CAC certificate; status report or registration details; Memorandum and Articles (companies)
Filing receipts or confirmation for each year
Tax ID confirmation; tax filing receipts; tax clearance certificate if obtained
Business account details; the last 12 monthly statements
NAFDAC certificates or SON certificates; label artwork; trademark documents
Tenancy or site use agreement; local government permits; fumigation certificate
Staff list, staff health or food handler certificates where required

blocks.text: How to organise it

items: Create a main folder on Google Drive (or similar) named, for example, "Rukky Bakes Compliance".
Inside it, create the eight numbered section folders from the table, so they always appear in order.
Scan or photograph each document clearly, save it as a PDF where possible, and name it with the date first: "2026-03 CAC status report.pdf".
Keep a printed set of the most-requested documents (certificate, status report, Tax ID, NAFDAC certificate) in a plastic file at your business.
Add a one-page index at the front listing each document, its date and its expiry or next due date.

blocks.title: Compliance pack gap check
items: Registration documents present
Annual returns up to date
Tax ID confirmed
Business account statements
Product approvals where needed
Monthly records kept
blocks.caption: Tick each line honestly; every unticked line becomes a task in your 90-day plan.

blocks.title: Worked example: a gap check
blocks.context: For example, Halima, who makes groundnut oil and kuli-kuli in Kaduna, builds her pack before applying for a bank loan.
steps: Registration: she has her business name certificate and registration details. Ticked.
Annual returns: none filed since registration last year. Gap: file on the portal this month.
Tax: she has never confirmed her Tax ID. Gap: confirm it through the official channel and record it in the pack.
Bank: she has 8 months of business account statements. Ticked, with a note to keep downloading monthly.
Product approvals: she has applied to NAFDAC for the oil but not the kuli-kuli. Gap: prepare the second application.
Records: monthly summaries exist for 5 of 8 months. Gap: rebuild the 3 missing months from bank statements and receipts.
blocks.result: Halima finds four gaps, each with a clear next action. She fixes the annual return and Tax ID first, because the bank asked for both.

blocks.title: Protect the pack
blocks.text: Your pack holds ID numbers, signatures and bank details. Use a strong password and two-step verification on the cloud account, do not post documents in group chats, and when you must send a document, send only that one, preferably as a PDF. Mark copies you send, for example "Copy for XYZ Supermarket vendor registration only".
If a document is lost or damaged

Do not panic. The CAC can issue **certified true copies** of registration documents on request through its official channels, for a fee. Bank statements can be downloaded again from your bank app or requested at a branch. NAFDAC and other regulators keep records of the certificates they issue. This is exactly why your index matters: it tells you the date and reference of each document, which makes replacement much faster.
Who usually asks for what

items: **Banks:** registration documents, ID of owners or directors, and bank statements.
**Supermarkets and retailers:** registration documents, NAFDAC certificates for each product, and account details.
**Corporate buyers:** registration documents, Tax ID, and sometimes tax clearance.
**Programmes and grants:** registration documents and a short business profile.
**Regulators on inspection:** product certificates, premises documents and staff health certificates.

blocks.text: Keep a ready-made "standard pack" PDF that joins your certificate, status report and Tax ID confirmation into one file. It answers most first requests in one message.

If you share responsibilities with a partner, co-director or family member, agree who updates the pack and when. One owner per section works well: for example, one person handles bank statements and records, and the other handles CAC filings and product certificates. Write those names on the index page.

Review the pack once a month, when you do your monthly summary. Add new statements and receipts, check expiry dates on certificates, and update the index. Ten minutes a month keeps it ready at all times.

takeaways: A compliance pack is one organised folder of every document proving your business is legal and up to date
Use eight numbered sections and name files with the date first
A gap check turns missing documents into clear tasks
Protect the pack with strong passwords and send documents only for a stated purpose

activity.title: Start your compliance pack
steps: Create the main folder and the eight numbered section folders.
Add every document you already have, named with the date first.
Write the one-page index with dates and expiry or due dates.
Do the gap check and list each gap with one next action.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of your folder structure, your index page, and your gap list with actions.

lessons.title: Using your registration to win customers, loans and support
objectives: Explain to a customer, bank or programme officer what your registration and compliance prove
Prepare the documents usually asked for in vendor registration and loan applications
Identify legitimate support channels such as SMEDAN and avoid fake grant offers
Present your business with a short, honest compliance statement

blocks.text: Registration costs time and money. It pays back when you use it. Most buyers, lenders and programmes care less about the certificate itself and more about what it signals: that you are real, traceable, organised and likely to deliver. Your job is to make that signal clear.
What different audiences want to see

head: Audience
What they usually ask for
What they want to know
rows: CAC documents, NAFDAC number for regulated products, bank details, sometimes Tax ID
Is the product approved and safe? Can we pay a business account?
CAC documents, Tax ID, bank details, sometimes tax clearance, references
Is this business real, and will it deliver on time?
CAC documents, bank statements, records, ID and BVN of owners or directors
Does money flow through the business regularly? Can it repay?
CAC documents, a short business description, sometimes records or a plan
Is this an active business that fits our criteria?

blocks.name: business-deal
blocks.alt: Two people closing a business deal
blocks.caption: Clear documents make it easy for a buyer to say yes.

blocks.text: Writing a short compliance statement

A compliance statement is a few honest sentences you can paste into an email, a WhatsApp message to a buyer, or a loan form. It says what is registered, what is up to date and what is in progress. Never claim something you do not have. Saying "NAFDAC application submitted" when it is true is far better than implying approval.

blocks.title: Worked example: a vendor registration message
blocks.context: For example, Funmi in Abeokuta wants to supply bottled zobo to a chain of three supermarkets. The purchasing officer asks for her details on WhatsApp.
steps: She opens her compliance pack and picks the four documents asked for: CAC certificate, status report, NAFDAC certificate for the zobo, and a bank letter or account details.

She writes: "Good afternoon. Funmi Drinks Ltd (RC number on the attached certificate) is registered with the CAC and up to date with annual returns. Our zobo drink is NAFDAC registered (number on label and certificate attached). Payments go to our company account at the bank shown. Our Tax ID confirmation is attached."
She sends the documents as clearly named PDFs, not blurry photos.
She adds a price list showing wholesale price per crate, minimum order and delivery days.
blocks.result: The purchasing officer can check everything quickly. Funmi looks organised, and her documents match what she said.

blocks.title: Where your business stands
items: Registered, records weak
Registered and organised
Unregistered, records weak
Unregistered, records good
blocks.caption: Buyers and lenders favour the top-right box: registered, compliant and organised.

blocks.text: Support channels, real and fake

**SMEDAN**, the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria, is the federal agency that supports micro, small and medium businesses with information, training, business development services and links to programmes. Its official website is smedan.gov.ng. State governments, banks, development partners and women's business associations also run programmes from time to time. Being registered, with records, puts you in a much stronger position when real opportunities appear.

blocks.title: Spot a fake grant
blocks.text: Be very careful with messages promising a grant or loan if you first pay a "processing fee", send your BVN and OTP, or click a link that is not on an official government domain. Real programmes are announced on official websites and verified social media pages, and they never ask for your bank PIN or OTP.
Getting loan-ready

Lenders lend against evidence of regular cash flow. Six to twelve months of business account statements showing steady income usually say more than any speech. Before you approach a bank or microfinance lender, prepare your compliance pack, a one-page summary of what the business sells and to whom, your monthly summaries, and a simple explanation of what the loan is for and how it will be repaid from sales.

items: Know exactly how much you need and what it will buy, with supplier quotes.
Show how the loan will increase sales or reduce costs.
Calculate the monthly repayment and check it against your monthly net profit.
Read every term, including fees and what happens if you miss a payment, before signing.
Avoid signing personal guarantees you do not fully understand.

blocks.text: After each pitch or application, note what was asked for and whether you had it ready. Over time this tells you which documents matter most for your kind of customer, and which gaps in your pack are costing you opportunities. Close those gaps first in your 90-day plan.

Finally, use your registration in your everyday branding. Put your registered business name, exactly as on the certificate, on invoices, receipts, labels and your WhatsApp Business profile. Consistency tells customers that the business behind the product is the one on the register.

takeaways: Buyers, lenders and programmes use registration as a signal that you are real, traceable and organised
Prepare the documents each audience usually asks for before they ask
A short, honest compliance statement wins trust; never imply approvals you do not have
Use official channels such as SMEDAN and never pay fees or share OTPs for a promised grant

activity.title: Write your compliance statement and pitch
steps: Write a four-sentence compliance statement about your business, using only true facts.
Choose one real buyer or lender you want to approach and list the documents they are likely to ask for.
Check your compliance pack for each document and mark any gaps.
Draft the WhatsApp or email message you would send them, with documents named clearly.
activity.evidence: Your compliance statement, the target audience's document list, and your draft message.

lessons.title: Your compliance calendar, final checklist and 90-day plan
objectives: Build a yearly compliance calendar with your own filing dates
Walk through filing an annual return when it falls due
Complete the certification checklist honestly
Write a 90-day plan that closes your biggest compliance gaps

blocks.text: Compliance becomes easy when it is scheduled. A calendar turns a vague worry into small tasks with dates. In this lesson you set up that calendar, see how an annual return filing works, complete the certification checklist and write your 90-day plan.

blocks.name: online-calendar
blocks.alt: A person planning on an online calendar
blocks.caption: Put every filing date on your phone calendar with a reminder a month before.

blocks.text: Your compliance calendar

head: When
Task
Where
rows: Download bank statement, write monthly summary, file receipts, update pack
Monthly (if you have staff or charge VAT)
Remit PAYE or file VAT as required
File tax return (personal for business name, company return for a company)
Renew NAFDAC registration, permits and certificates

blocks.text: Check exact due dates for each filing on the official portals when you set up your calendar, and set two reminders for each: one month before and one week before. If you use an accountant or agent, put the dates in your own calendar too. You are the one responsible.
Filing your annual return when it is due

items: Log into the CAC portal with the account used for registration.
Open your business or company and choose the annual returns service.
Confirm or update details: address, proprietors or directors, shareholders and PSCs.
Enter or upload the financial information asked for, using your yearly figures from your records.
Pay the fee shown on the portal, download the confirmation and save it in Section 2 of your pack.

blocks.text: Certification checklist

items: I have chosen my business structure and can explain why.
My business is registered with the CAC, or my application is submitted, with evidence.
I have confirmed my Tax ID status through an official channel.
I have a business bank account, or a dated plan to open one.
I have checked whether my products need NAFDAC or SON, with evidence of the decision.
I have kept records for at least one month and produced a monthly summary.
My compliance pack exists with an index and a gap list.
I have a compliance calendar with reminders set.

blocks.title: A 90-day compliance plan
items: Days 1 to 30: register or fix
Days 31 to 60: tax and bank
Days 61 to 90: products and records
Day 90: review and update pack
blocks.caption: Break your gaps into three monthly blocks so progress is steady and visible.

blocks.title: Worked example: Esther's 90-day plan
blocks.context: For example, Esther runs a small bakery in Ibadan. Her gap check shows: business name not yet registered, no Tax ID confirmation, money going into her personal account, no NAFDAC registration for her packaged cookies, and records kept only on and off.
steps: Days 1 to 30: register the business name on the CAC portal (budget from the fee shown on the portal), and start daily sales and expense records.
Days 31 to 60: confirm her Tax ID, open a business account, and move all customer payments to it. Write her first two monthly summaries.
Days 61 to 90: fix her cookie label, gather MSME documents and apply to NAFDAC for one product. Write her third monthly summary.
Day 90: update the compliance pack, set calendar reminders for her first annual return and tax filing, and review progress against the plan.
blocks.result: In 90 days Esther moves from informal to registered, banked and organised, with one product in the NAFDAC process and every future filing on her calendar.

blocks.text: Getting help when you need it

You do not have to do everything alone. A chartered accountant can prepare yearly accounts and tax returns from your records. An accredited agent can handle company filings and changes. The CAC, NRS, your state tax authority and NAFDAC all have official help channels listed on their websites. SMEDAN and women's business associations can point you to training. Use help to save time, but keep control: your login, your email, your documents and your calendar.

Before you submit your capstone, show your compliance pack and plan to one person you trust, such as a mentor, an accountant or a fellow learner. Ask them two questions: what is missing, and what is unclear. Write down their answers, decide what you will change, and include that short reflection in your submission.

At day 90, compare where you are with where you started. Count how many gaps from your first gap check are now closed, and write the new list of remaining gaps. That becomes your next 90-day plan, so compliance becomes a steady routine rather than a one-time rush.

blocks.title: Keep the plan honest
blocks.text: If a task slips, move it with a new date and a reason rather than ticking it. An honest plan that is 80 percent done is worth more than a perfect plan that hides gaps.

takeaways: A compliance calendar turns yearly and monthly duties into dated tasks with reminders
Annual returns are filed on the CAC portal using details and figures from your records
The certification checklist proves you can apply what you learned to your own business
A 90-day plan closes your biggest gaps in three monthly blocks

activity.title: Set your calendar and write your 90-day plan
steps: Add every task from the compliance calendar to your phone calendar with two reminders each.
Work through the certification checklist and mark each item done or not done.
Write your 90-day plan in three blocks, using your gap list from the compliance pack.
Share the plan with one person who will check on your progress at day 45 and day 90.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of your calendar entries, your completed checklist and your written 90-day plan.

quiz.q: A purchasing officer asks Funmi for proof her zobo can be sold in supermarkets. Which document matters most for the product itself?
options: The NAFDAC registration certificate for the zobo
quiz.explain: Packaged drinks need NAFDAC registration before retail sale, so the product's NAFDAC certificate is the key proof.

quiz.q: Halima's gap check shows four gaps, and her bank has asked for her annual return and Tax ID. What should she do first?
options: Apply for NAFDAC for a new product
Fix the annual return and Tax ID
Wait until all four gaps can be fixed together
quiz.explain: Fix the gaps that block the immediate opportunity first. The bank asked for both, so those come before other tasks.

quiz.q: You receive a message: "Federal women's grant of 2 million naira, pay 15,000 naira processing fee and send your OTP." What is the right response?
options: Pay quickly before slots run out
Send the OTP but not the fee
Treat it as a likely scam and check only official sources
Forward it to all your groups
quiz.explain: Real programmes do not ask for processing fees to a personal account or for your OTP. Verify on official websites only.

quiz.q: Which file name follows the compliance pack naming rule best?
quiz.explain: Putting the date first and describing the document makes files sort in order and easy to find.

quiz.q: Esther's NAFDAC application slipped from day 70 to day 85. What should she do in her plan?
options: Move it with a new date and note the reason
Start a new plan from day 1
quiz.explain: An honest plan records slips with new dates and reasons, so the gap stays visible until it is closed.

quiz.q: When should reminders for a yearly filing like the CAC annual return be set?
options: One month before and one week before
quiz.explain: Two reminders, a month and a week before, give time to gather figures and file without penalties.

finalQuiz.q: Which law governs business name and company registration in Nigeria?
finalQuiz.explain: CAMA 2020 is the main law on registering business names, companies and other entities with the CAC.

finalQuiz.q: Two friends plan a catering business that will sign contracts with event centres and may face large claims if something goes wrong. Which structure fits best?
options: A business name in one friend's name
A private limited company with both as shareholders and directors
finalQuiz.explain: A limited company gives limited liability and shows both owners clearly, which suits higher-risk contract work.

finalQuiz.q: Under CAMA 2020, what is the minimum issued share capital for a private company at the time of writing?
finalQuiz.explain: CAMA 2020 sets 100,000 naira as the minimum issued share capital for a private company.

finalQuiz.q: What should you check first before filling the business name form on the CAC portal?
finalQuiz.explain: The name check comes first; the form depends on an approved name.

finalQuiz.q: A company has 2,000,000 shares. Bola holds 500,000. What share of the company does she own?
finalQuiz.explain: 500,000 divided by 2,000,000 equals 0.25, which is 25 percent.

finalQuiz.q: At the time of writing, how are individuals identified under Nigeria's new Tax ID system?
options: By their CAC BN number only
finalQuiz.explain: Under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 reforms, individuals are identified through their NIN and registered businesses through their CAC number.

finalQuiz.q: Rukayat receives customer payments into her personal account and buys supplies from it too. What is the main compliance problem?
options: It is illegal to own a personal account
Business and personal money are mixed, so records and filings are unreliable
finalQuiz.explain: Mixing money makes it hard to prove sales, costs and profit for tax, annual returns and loans.

finalQuiz.q: Grace never filed annual returns for her company. What is a likely consequence when a hotel asks for her status report?
options: The status shows the company is not up to date, and she must catch up and pay penalties
Her company becomes a business name
finalQuiz.explain: Missed returns build up penalties and affect the company's status, which buyers and banks check.

finalQuiz.q: Ifeyinwa wants to sell packaged pepper sauce in supermarkets. What does NAFDAC's MSME procedure require along with documents and payment?
options: A facility inspection and laboratory analysis of samples
finalQuiz.explain: The MSME route includes a facility inspection at which samples are taken for lab analysis before approval.

finalQuiz.q: Which label statement should be removed from a new body cream?
options: Ingredients listed in order of quantity
finalQuiz.explain: Unproven medical claims mislead buyers and are not allowed without evidence and approval.

finalQuiz.q: A small company qualifies for 0 percent company income tax under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. Which statement is correct?
options: It no longer needs to file returns
It must still file its returns
It must convert to a business name
It must pay VAT at 30 percent instead
finalQuiz.explain: A zero rate does not remove the filing duty. Filing proves compliance and supports tax clearance.

finalQuiz.q: Which item belongs in the "Days 1 to 30" block of a 90-day plan for an unregistered business?
options: Register with the CAC and start daily records
finalQuiz.explain: Registration and daily records are the foundation that every later task depends on, so they come first.

capstone.title: Business compliance pack and 90-day plan
capstone.brief: Build a complete compliance pack for your own business (or a real business you support): your structure decision, registration evidence or a completed application, Tax ID status, bank set-up, product regulator decision with an honest label draft, at least one month of records with a monthly summary, a compliance calendar, a reflection on feedback and a 90-day plan.
steps: Write a one-page structure decision: business name or limited company, with reasons based on risk, owners and growth plans.
Register on the CAC portal, or complete every step up to payment, and save screenshots of each stage.
Confirm your Tax ID status through an official channel and record the result.
Open a business bank account, or write a dated plan to open one, and route business payments into it.
Decide whether each product needs NAFDAC, SON or neither, and draft an honest, complete label for one product.
Keep sales and expense records for at least one month and produce a monthly summary with gross margin.
Assemble the eight-section compliance pack with an index, do a gap check, and set a compliance calendar with reminders.
Show the pack to one person (a mentor, accountant or fellow learner), note their feedback, and write a short reflection and your 90-day plan.
evidence: CAC certificate or screenshots of the completed application
Note of Tax ID status from an official channel
Bank account evidence or dated plan
Product regulator decision and label draft
One month of records and a monthly summary with calculations
